subject: Brightline launch capacity request — quota scenarios & product asks
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@brightlinehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Launch traffic forecast + temporary quota increase request

Hi Irene —

We’re ramping up to our feature launch on 2027-05-15 and need help ensuring calls don’t get throttled on day one. Attached is a traffic workbook (summary below).

Key ask: a temporary per-customer quota increase for the first 72 hours around launch plus a burst allowance during the peak hour.

Forecast summary (expected peak day):
- Peak concurrent requests: 4,200 reqs/min (70 reqs/sec)
- Avg tokens per request: 750 tokens
- Expected sustained window at peak: 2 hours, with a 20-minute spike where requests double
- Pilot length: 90 days (May–Aug), with immediate priority on the May 15th launch

What we need from Redwood:
1) Confirmation that the hosted API can handle a temporary bump to ~5k reqs/min for Brightline for launch day (we can do canary ramp if helpful)
2) Any recommended throttling/smoothing settings or warmup guidance (we can adjust client-side)
3) Lead time for any Dedicated pool reservation if needed

We’re open to an entitlement/commit model if it helps you prioritize capacity. Happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Thanks —
Sam
Sam Carter
Head of Integrations, Brightline Health
ops@brightlinehealth.com

Attachment: brightline_traffic_model_v2.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Launch traffic forecast + temporary quota increase request

Team — forwarding Brightline’s request (below). High level: customer asks for a 72h bump around May 15 and a burst window for the peak spike.

Product / ops questions I need help on before I respond to Sam:
- Neha: what headroom do we actually have on hosted pools in us-west for the week of 5/15? Can we provide a temporary soft limit of 2x–3x per-customer for a 72h window without impacting other customers? If not, what mitigation (rate shaping/cache) should we propose?
- David: if we need deterministic performance, what’s the minimum lead time to provision a small Dedicated reservation for the pilot? Also, any routing we should configure (region pinning, fallback model variants) to avoid noisy neighbor effects?
- Karthik/Monica: commercial tie-ins — would Brightline consider a short reserved commit for the pilot if we can guarantee throughput? We should decide an ask I can take to them.

I’ll draft two options to present to them:
A) Fast path: soft hosted bump + client-side smoothing + runbook (48–72h notice)
B) Deterministic path: Dedicated reservation + SLA exception for launch (needs ~72h provisioning + commercial commit)

Proposed next step: quick 30-minute sync today or tomorrow to align.

Thanks —
Irene
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Launch traffic forecast + temporary quota increase request

Irene — quick commercial context: Brightline is a mid-market customer with clear expansion potential (healthcare vertical). For the pilot they’d likely accept a 90-day pilot commit if we provide predictable performance for the launch window.

Suggested negotiation posture:
- Offer the soft hosted bump as the default (low friction) and include a 90-day pilot commit tied to lower burst pricing if they sign before launch.
- If they need hard guarantees for the day-of traffic, propose a small Dedicated reservation (we can price the 90-day slot as an add-on).

I can lead pricing if we agree to the options — I’ll draft commercial language for the customer-facing runbook. For now, ask the infra/capacity folks what hard limits we can promise so we don’t overcommit.

Karthik
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Launch traffic forecast + temporary quota increase request — capacity notes

Thanks for the heads up, Irene. I reviewed Brightline’s workbook and ran the forecast against our current pool utilization in us-west. Summary and options below.

Current hosted headroom (us-west pools):
- Baseline spare capacity: ~40% across serving clusters this week, but does not guarantee per-customer burst in a single tenant under 1-minute spikes.
- We can provision a controlled soft increase (per-customer quota) to roughly 2x current per-customer default for a 48–72h window with minimal risk, provided we also apply client-side smoothing and prefix caching.

Options (risk vs lead time):
1) Soft hosted bump (fast; 24–48h internal coordination)
   - Increase per-customer request limit from 200 rps -> 1,200 rps (sustained), allow 2,500 rps short bursts (20-minute windows)
   - Requires runbook + client-side backoff guidance; recommend warmup ramp over 30 minutes during peak
   - No Dedicated reservation; lower SLA guarantee (best-effort)

2) Dedicated reservation (deterministic; 72h+ prep and infra approval)
   - Provision a small reserved pool sized for 3k–4k reqs/min sustained for the launch window
   - Full routing pin, stronger latency SLOs, and isolation from noisy neighbors
   - Requires commercial commit and capacity ops coordination (we need purchase order or signed addendum)

3) Hybrid: soft hosted bump + fallback to lighter model variant for overflow
   - Configure routing policy to fallback to a lower memory/quantized variant (slightly degraded quality) after X% utilization to preserve availability

Attachments: I’m attaching a short runbook with recommended client-side patterns and suggested SLOs (temp-burst-runbook.md). Also flagged the SLA exception PDF to legal for a quick review.

Next steps:
- If Sales prefers soft path, I’ll schedule the hosted bump and prep the runbook (need BU approval 24h before change).
- If Sales prefers deterministic guarantee, David, we’ll need your team to confirm provisioning timeline and ops checklist.

-Neha
Senior Manager, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, ops@brightlinehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-28T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch traffic forecast + temporary quota increase request — proposed plan

Hi Sam — thanks for the workbook and context. Quick internal alignment and our recommended approach below.

What we can offer for May 15 launch:
- Fast path (recommended initial): Temporary hosted quota bump with client-side smoothing. We will:
  * Raise Brightline’s per-customer limit to 1,200 rps sustained, allow 2,500 rps short bursts (20-minute windows) for the first 72 hours around 5/15.
  * Provide a runbook with warmup ramp guidance and backoff patterns (attached) and a private Slack channel for real-time ops during the window.
  * This requires a 48-hour internal notice to schedule the bump and we’ll need a launch-day point of contact from Brightline (ops@brightlinehealth.com is fine).

- Deterministic path (if you need strict guarantees): We can provision a small Dedicated reservation sized for the peak, but it requires a signed pilot addendum and ~72 hours lead time. Karthik can run pricing and contract details if you want to go this route.

Immediate asks from Brightline to proceed:
1) Confirm you want us to schedule the hosted bump for the 72-hour window starting 2027-05-15 09:00 PDT
2) Provide a launch-day SOS contact and Slack handle
3) Confirm whether you want to pursue Dedicated (Karthik will follow up on commercial terms)

We’ll act on your reply. If you want, we can do a 30-minute runbook walkthrough tomorrow (Irene + Neha + David + Karthik + Monica + your ops lead).

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Attachments: temp-burst-runbook.md, sla-exception-request.pdf
